title: AUGUR app manifest
description: An app's manifest.json: what the registry accepts when the app registers (PUT /v1/apps/{id}). Generated from the registry's schema by pnpm manifest-schema; check a manifest with node scripts/check-manifests.mjs <manifest.json>.

$schema.description: Where editors find this schema, contracts/manifest.schema.json: a path or an address. The registry doesn't use it.

id.description: The app's id, such as "board"; its route, client and storage are named after it

route.description: Route prefix the shell maps to this app

entry.description: URL of the app's ES module entry: a path on AUGUR (/apps/…) or a full https address. No backslashes or control characters.

sdk.description: The @augur/mfe-sdk releases the app works with, a semver range such as ^1.0.0. The shell will not open an app whose range its SDK does not satisfy.

description.description: One line shown under the app name in the shell

requiredRole.description: Only people with this role can open it

handles.description: Intent types this app handles, such as document.open

ai.description: The app is an AI; the menus draw it as a bubble

search.description: The app's service answers GET /v1/search?q=, and the shell's Find asks it

storage.description: The storage the app keeps on AUGUR: its own database schema, its own bucket. See docs/app-storage.md

maxUpload.description: The largest request body, in MB, the gateway lets through to the app's service; 10 without it. An admin can lower it.

detail.description: A sentence on what it changes, for the person choosing it

until.description: Its last day, YYYY-MM-DD; after it, it's off for everyone and Admin says the app should drop it or ship it

previews.description: Features the app has ready to try before they're everyone's (SDK 1.7): admins say who gets each, people opt in, and the app asks ctx.previewOn(id)

id.description: How the app's service names it: "retentionDays"

detail.description: A sentence on what it changes

unit.description: What the number counts, shown after it: "days"

settings.description: Settings the app offers admins in Admin, Apps; its service reads them from the registry

scopes.description: What the app's service asks to do on AUGUR, such as "notifications:send". An app may always register itself.

floors.description: The kinds of floor the app works on; every kind without it

floor.description: "team" means any team, at any depth

module.description: The module the app's entry exposes for it

role.description: Only for people with this role on the floor

rollup.description: Shows this floor and the teams below it that the person is on, using AUGUR's roll-up

surfaces.description: What the app shows on each kind of floor, for the shell to place. Each surface's floor must be in floors.

orbit.description: false: the app keeps its own menu inside it and the shell never shows its Orbit

sameOnEveryFloor.description: true: the app shows the same on every floor, so the shell's floor gauge rests while it's open and says why (SDK 1.6)

followsAddress.description: true: the app follows the address itself, so the shell keeps it mounted on Back and Forward inside it (SDK 1.11)

focus.description: true: the app can narrow what it shows to a working context, from ctx.focus (SDK 1.10). Reserved: nothing sets one yet (ADR 0029)

category.description: The kind of app it says it is (SDK 1.11, ADR 0032). Only honoured for apps that ship with AUGUR or come from its app feed

icon.description: A UI kit icon name, not the app's own

detail.description: One line on what's in it

areas.description: The broad parts of what the app covers, which Title lists under it (SDK 1.5). Menu groups name theirs in area. See docs/shell-principles.md

area.description: The id of the app's area the group belongs to (SDK 1.5)

detail.description: One short fact, never a sentence

keywords.description: Extra words search finds it by

path.description: Where in the app it opens, below the app's route

menu.description: The app's menu, shown by the shell as Orbit at the app's root. A group with one item opens it directly
